scenes.tts: How does one small change at a synapse become a correction that arrives on time?
scenes.visual: Title card fades. One blue parallel-fibre synapse on a Purkinje dendrite, with a red climbing fibre beside it. The question appears.
scenes.narration: How does one small change at a synapse become a correction that arrives on time?

scenes.tts: David Marr and James Albus proposed that the climbing fibre is a teacher. But which way would it change a synapse?
scenes.visual: Caption cards: David Marr, 1969. James Albus, 1971. The red climbing fibre is labelled teacher.
scenes.narration: David Marr and James Albus proposed that the climbing fibre is a teacher. But which way would it change a synapse?

scenes.tts: Marr guessed stronger. Albus guessed weaker.
scenes.visual: Two arrows by the synapse: Marr, stronger (up); Albus, weaker (down). A question mark between them.
scenes.narration: Marr guessed stronger. Albus guessed weaker.

scenes.tts: In 1982, Masao Ito and Masanobu Kano tested it in rabbits. Compare three conditions.
scenes.visual: Caption card: Ito and Kano, 1982, rabbit cerebellum. Three empty panels appear side by side.
scenes.narration: In 1982, Masao Ito and Masanobu Kano tested it in rabbits. Compare three conditions.

scenes.tts: Parallel fibres alone. No lasting depression.
scenes.visual: Panel 1: parallel-fibre stimulation only. Its response trace shows no lasting drop. Small note: these test conditions differ from those used to induce strengthening.
scenes.narration: Parallel fibres alone. No lasting depression.

scenes.tts: Climbing fibre alone. No lasting depression either.
scenes.caption: Climbing fibre alone. No lasting depression either.
scenes.visual: Panel 2: climbing-fibre stimulation only. Its parallel-fibre response trace shows no lasting pairing-like depression.
scenes.narration: Climbing fibre alone. No lasting depression either.

scenes.tts: The two together. Afterwards the parallel fibre response is smaller, and it stays smaller for at least an hour.
scenes.caption: The two together. Afterwards the parallel-fibre response is smaller, and it stays smaller for at least an hour.
scenes.visual: Panel 3: both inputs paired. The response trace shrinks and stays small; the time axis runs past 1 hour.
scenes.narration: The two together. Afterwards the parallel-fibre response is smaller, and it stays smaller for at least an hour.

scenes.tts: Under these conditions, only pairing weakened the synapse. This is cerebellar long term depression, the sign Albus had chosen.
scenes.caption: Under these conditions, only pairing weakened the synapse. This is cerebellar long-term depression, the sign Albus had chosen.
scenes.visual: Panel 3 is highlighted and labelled long-term depression (LTD). Albus's down arrow lights.
scenes.narration: Under these conditions, only pairing weakened the synapse. This is cerebellar long-term depression, the sign Albus had chosen.

scenes.tts: The input to a brake gets weaker. Does the nucleus fire more, or less?
scenes.visual: A three-step strip: synapse dims, then a Purkinje cell, then a nucleus. The last box shows a question mark.
scenes.narration: The input to a brake gets weaker. Does the nucleus fire more, or less?

scenes.tts: More, with other inputs unchanged. The foot presses the brake less, so the nucleus, already running, speeds up. Two negatives make a positive.
scenes.visual: The strip completes: synapse weaker, Purkinje cell fires less, nucleus fires more. Small note beside the strip: other inputs unchanged. A foot eases off a brake pedal. Label: two negatives make a positive.
scenes.narration: More, with other inputs unchanged. The foot presses the brake less, so the nucleus, already running, speeds up. Two negatives make a positive.

scenes.tts: But which parallel fibres are weakened? It depends on the region. In the flocculus, it is those active about a hundred and twenty milliseconds before the climbing fibre.
scenes.visual: A timeline: a row of parallel fibres fire in sequence. The red climbing-fibre spike comes later; the fibres that fired a beat earlier are highlighted. Label: mouse flocculus, about 120 ms; other regions differ.
scenes.narration: But which parallel fibres are weakened? It depends on the region. In the flocculus, it is those active about a hundred and twenty milliseconds before the climbing fibre.

scenes.tts: That matters, because a visual error reaches the flocculus roughly a tenth of a second after the mistake.
scenes.visual: On the timeline, a mark: mistake made. A later mark: visual error signal reaches the flocculus, roughly 0.1 s later.
scenes.narration: That matters, because a visual error reaches the flocculus roughly a tenth of a second after the mistake.

scenes.tts: So the fibres active just before carry the context in which the mistake was made.
scenes.visual: The highlighted fibres sit under the mistake made mark. Label: the context when the mistake was made.
scenes.narration: So the fibres active just before carry the context in which the mistake was made.

scenes.tts: Next time that context arrives, the learned change can act before the late visual error does. The correction need not wait for feedback.
scenes.visual: A second trial on the same timeline: the nucleus output bumps up ahead of where the error mark came before. Label: schematic; exact timing depends on the circuit.
scenes.narration: Next time that context arrives, the learned change can act before the late visual error does. The correction need not wait for feedback.

scenes.tts: What does learning look like in a real cell? Monkeys returned a handle to a set position, and then the load changed.
scenes.visual: A monkey's hand on a handle; a load arrow pushes it, then a different load arrow. Caption card: Gilbert and Thach, 1977.
scenes.narration: What does learning look like in a real cell? Monkeys returned a handle to a set position, and then the load changed.

scenes.tts: Climbing fibre events show as big complex spikes; ordinary output spikes are simple spikes. In some recorded cells, complex spikes grew more frequent as the monkeys adapted. Simple spike responses fell, and stayed lower.
scenes.caption: Climbing-fibre events show as big complex spikes; ordinary output spikes are simple spikes. In some recorded cells, complex spikes grew more frequent as the monkeys adapted. Simple-spike responses fell, and stayed lower.
scenes.visual: A raster fills in, one row per trial: thin ticks for simple spikes, heavy marks for complex spikes. After the load change, heavy marks cluster; later rows show fewer thin ticks. Label: schematic of some recorded cells.
scenes.narration: Climbing-fibre events show as big complex spikes; ordinary output spikes are simple spikes. In some recorded cells, complex spikes grew more frequent as the monkeys adapted. Simple-spike responses fell, and stayed lower.

scenes.tts: That pattern fits the rule, though it does not measure the synapse directly.
scenes.visual: Two labels on the raster: more error signals; lasting drop in response. Beneath: fits the model, not a synapse measurement.
scenes.narration: That pattern fits the rule, though it does not measure the synapse directly.

scenes.tts: But depression alone can only release the brake. What if the output needs to fall instead?
scenes.visual: The brake strip again, with a down arrow on the nucleus output and a question mark.
scenes.narration: But depression alone can only release the brake. What if the output needs to fall instead?

scenes.tts: One way: strengthen the same synapses, so the brake presses harder. Parallel fibre activity without a paired climbing fibre can do that. Other circuit changes can also lower output.
scenes.caption: One way: strengthen the same synapses, so the brake presses harder. Parallel-fibre activity without a paired climbing fibre can do that. Other circuit changes can also lower output.
scenes.visual: The synapse brightens when blue fibres fire with no red spike. Label: long-term potentiation, one route. The brake presses harder and the nucleus slows.
scenes.narration: One way: strengthen the same synapses, so the brake presses harder. Parallel-fibre activity without a paired climbing fibre can do that. Other circuit changes can also lower output.

scenes.tts: In this one simplified channel, weakening alone can only raise the output, with other inputs fixed. Strengthening can reverse that change.
scenes.visual: Two example target curves in one simplified channel, other inputs fixed: output up, and output down. A weaken-only rule fits the first and stays flat on the second. Label: one fixed-sign channel only.
scenes.narration: In this one simplified channel, weakening alone can only raise the output, with other inputs fixed. Strengthening can reverse that change.

scenes.tts: The rule has limits. The teacher works in some tasks and not others. Mice without detectable depression still learned the tested tasks. Climbing fibres also signal reward.
scenes.visual: Three small cards: teacher gated by the task; learning without detectable LTD; climbing fibres also signal reward.
scenes.narration: The rule has limits. The teacher works in some tasks and not others. Mice without detectable depression still learned the tested tasks. Climbing fibres also signal reward.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: in this model, a well-timed error signal can weaken the eligible synapses. With other inputs fixed, less brake means more output, ready before the late feedback next time.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: A well-timed error signal can weaken eligible synapses. Less brake, more output (other inputs fixed), ahead of late feedback. Unpaired parallel-fibre activity can do the reverse. Small print: timing depends on region and protocol; mouse flocculus, about 120 ms.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: in this model, a well-timed error signal can weaken the eligible synapses. With other inputs fixed, less brake means more output, ready before the late feedback next time.
